name: Phone at eye level / tech neck avoidance
lead: Holding a phone at eye level to avoid tech neck, also called text neck, is a posture habit meant to prevent the head-down, forward-head position associated with prolonged device use. In looksmaxxing and posture communities it is linked to neck posture and jawline appearance.
A 2023 scoping review found that text neck is widely called a global epidemic but lacks a consensus definition across the peer-reviewed literature [1].
Related work has examined questionnaires on symptoms and preventive measures [2], skin changes sometimes labeled tech neck lines [3], and posture changes in skeletal remains [7].
infobox: Text neck, tech neck, forward head posture

paras: A scoping review of peer-reviewed articles using the terms text neck or tech neck found inconsistent definitions, which the authors said challenges researchers and clinicians [1]. Wikipedia's article on forward head posture describes smartphone and laptop use as a commonly proposed contributor, presented as plausible rather than established causation [4].

No studies found testing holding a phone at eye level as an intervention. Related research exists. A 2025 pilot questionnaire study explored symptoms, posture and preventive measures such as breaks and ergonomic tools [2]. A 2023 open-label study examined a topical and device treatment for tech neck lines and wrinkles in Chinese women, addressing skin rather than posture [3]. A 2024 study examined instrument-assisted soft tissue mobilization in tech neck [5]. A 2024 preprint compared bone changes at the skull base in modern and ancient populations in relation to tech neck posture [7]. Reviews in 2026 discussed tech neck as a spinal and orthodontic topic [6].

Wikipedia notes claims that head-forward posture increases neck load several-fold and ties it to neck pain, and cites a 2019 meta-analysis finding correlation between forward head posture and neck pain in adults but not adolescents; it does not discuss jawline or facial appearance [4].

card.summary: Keeping the phone high to avoid head-down posture; tech neck itself lacks an agreed definition.
card.note: No studies found testing the habit itself.

quick.overview:
This habit means lifting your phone toward eye level so your head does not tilt down. It is discussed to avoid tech neck and its alleged effect on neck and jaw look.

Research on tech neck is early and a 2023 review found no consensus definition. No study tests the habit.
quick.mechanism: The reasoning is biomechanical: a head held forward and down is said to load the neck more than an upright head.
quick.risks: No notable risks are described. Holding a phone higher is a behavioral change only.
